stories.title: Come Back, Cat!
stories.credit: "Come back, Cat!" written by Nicola Rijsdijk, illustrated by Karen Lilje, (c) Book Dash 2014, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/105115-come-back-cat). 바꾼 점: 글 없는 쪽 하나를 빼고 마지막 쪽에 한 문장을 더했으며, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Come back, cat! Play with me.
Sit in your basket. Stay right here!
Come back, cat! That's way too high.
Come back, cat! Don't go outside.
Come back, cat! That's not yours.
Come back, cat. What have you got?
Come back, cat. That's not your friend!
Hello, cat! Are you back?
Stay in your basket. It's nap time now.
Cat?
There you are, cat. Shh. Nap time.

stories.title: The Bee and the Elephant
stories.credit: "The Bee and the Elephant" by Long Ravy, translated by Celia Bolam, illustrated by Try Samphos, (c) Room to Read 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/37232-the-bee-and-the-elephant). 바꾼 점: 쪽 나눔 그대로, 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: "I am lost," said Little Bee. "I cannot find my home! Can you please help me, Mr. Elephant?"
"Is this nest your home, Little Bee?" the elephant asked.
"Oh no!" cried Little Bee. "This is a bird's home."
"Is this cave your home?" asked the elephant.
"Oh no! This is a bat's home."
"Is this hive your home, Little Bee?"
"Oh yes!" said Little Bee happily. "This is my home."
"Thank you for helping me, Mr. Elephant."

stories.title: The Three Little Kittens
stories.credit: "The Three Little Kittens" by Chou Chinith, translated by Magdalena Cooper, illustrated by Youm Kosal, (c) Room to Read 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/36641-the-three-little-kittens). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: One day three little kittens meet a big dog.
The kittens are scared of the dog.
The little kittens run...
...and the dog follows them.
The little kittens run faster and faster!
The little kittens run into a little bird.
But the little kittens keep on running.
The little kittens run into a little boy.
But the little kittens keep on running.
They run towards a long piece of wood.
"Uh oh! We're in trouble now." "Help! Help!" they cry.
The smiling dog runs up to them. "I'm so happy to run with all of you!" he says.
What a surprise! Now, the little kittens have a new friend.

stories.title: The Race
stories.credit: "The Race" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Kavya Singh and Natasha Mehra, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/12294-the-race). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Four friends want to have a race with their toys.
Veena has a green car. Meena has a yellow auto.
Sanju has a red bus. Manju has a blue lorry.
Ready, one, two, three, go! Here comes Lucky. Ha-ha, Lucky has joined the race.
Look, look! Lucky is the fastest of them all. Lucky wins the race.

stories.title: Fat King Thin Dog
stories.credit: "Fat King Thin Dog" written and illustrated by Parismita, (c) Pratham Books 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/7-fat-king-thin-dog). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고 그림 크기를 줄였으며, 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: This is a fat king.
The fat king has a thin dog. The fat king and his thin dog go for a walk.
The dog sees a bird. The dog runs after the bird.
The king runs after the dog.
They run and run. They run and run for many days.
The king catches the dog.
Now the fat king is thin.

stories.title: Ting Tong
stories.credit: "Ting Tong" written by Lubaina Bandukwala, illustrated by Zainab Tambawalla, (c) Pratham Books 2011, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/15458-ting-tong). 바꾼 점: 소리 흉내말의 대문자를 소문자로 바꾸고 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Whenever I try to sleep,
Ting tong! The doorbell rings.
Now I turn the other side, and...
Buzz, buzz, the mobile goes.
Once again, I give it a try,
and this time it's a... dong!
Tring, tring! What was that?
A bicycle rushing by!
"What?" says Mamma, seeing me up. "Aren't you asleep still?"
"But Mamma," I tell her with my eyes, "how can I sleep?"
"Ting, buzz, dong, tring! The whole house is full of rings!"

stories.title: Clever Pig
stories.credit: "Clever Pig" written by Nathalie Koenig, illustrated by Josh Morgan, (c) Book Dash 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/19085-clever-pig). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고, 음성 안전검사가 잘못 걸러 낸 6·13·16쪽 문장을 조금 바꾸고(little 추가 등), 글 없는 마지막 두 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Come, Pig! Let's play.
Can you find the carrot?
No, it's not under there.
No, it's not inside.
Clever Pig!
Wake up, little Pig! Let's play. Where did she go?
Pig is gone.
The sun came up.
And the sun went down. But, no Pig.
I miss my friend.
My Pig! Clever Pig.
And one, two, three new friends!
Come, little pigs!
Let's play.
Time for bed!
Good night, little pigs.

stories.title: Counting Animals
stories.credit: "Counting Animals" written by Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi, illustrated by Rob Owen, (c) African Storybook Initiative 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/14790-counting-animals). 바꾼 점: 7쪽의 물음 한 문장(사자를 누가 무서워할까?)을 빼고 그림 크기를 줄였으며, 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: One elephant is going to drink water.
Two giraffes are going to drink water.
Three buffaloes and four birds are also going to drink water.
Five antelopes and warthogs are walking to the water.
Seven zebras are running to the water.
Eight frogs and nine fish are swimming in the water.
One lion roars. He also wants to drink.
One elephant is drinking water with the lion.

stories.title: Gorillas Go to the Beach
stories.credit: "Gorillas Go to the Beach" written and illustrated by Jemma Jose, (c) Pratham Books 2019, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/56310-gorillas-go-to-the-beach). 바꾼 점: 'bhutta(인도식 구운 옥수수)'를 'corn'으로 바꾸고 글 없는 마지막 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: The gorillas are off to the beach. Gorillas dig in the sand.
Gorilla jumps in the water. Splash!
Gorilla eats yummy corn from the food carts.
Gorillas throw a frisbee on the shore.
Gorilla plays with a friendly dog.
Gorilla collects shells to show her friends.
Gorillas are tired. Now it's time to watch the moon rise.

stories.title: I Can Climb!
stories.credit: "I Can Climb!" written by Mini Shrinivasan, illustrated by Deval Maniar, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/822-i-can-climb). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I am a big boy now.
I can climb up the steps.
But I cannot climb down again.
I can climb on a chair.
But I cannot climb down again.
I climb on to the chair, and then on the table!
But I cannot climb down again.
"Papa! Papa!" I shout. Papa laughs. "Sonu, learn to climb down!" he says.
I am afraid. But I do not cry.
Slowly, I get down from the table, and down from the chair.
At last, I have learnt to climb down too!

stories.title: Who Is It?
stories.credit: "Who Is It?" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Pratyush Gupta, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/11986-who-is-it). 바꾼 점: 그림이 없는 첫 쪽에는 표지 그림을, 마지막 쪽에는 앞 쪽 그림을 씀, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Priya hears a sound. Srrr... srrr... Who is it?
Priya runs out. She sees the cow chewing grass. No, it is not the cow that is making the sound.
Is it the monkey in the tree? No, it is not the monkey.
Is it the frog hopping in the grass? No, it is not the frog.
Is it the deer jumping along? No, it is not the deer.
Is it the fish in the pond? No, it is not the fish.
Then Priya sees the elephant! The elephant is rubbing its back against a tree.
Now Priya has her answer! Srrr... srrr...

stories.title: The Mango Tree
stories.credit: "The Mango Tree" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Kavya Singh, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/11537-the-mango-tree). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: We like to visit Grandma's village.
Grandma has a big mango tree in her garden. Many birds come there.
I like to hide in the mango tree. No one can see me here.
Father looks for me near the well. Mother looks for me near the cowshed. But no one can find me.
Oh no! At last Grandma's dog finds me.
Now I have to climb down. Grandma gives me a big hug.

stories.title: Piggy Wants to Fly
stories.credit: "Piggy Wants to Fly" by Mut Kunthy, translated by Stephanie Wei, illustrated by Youm Kosal, (c) Room to Read 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/37233-piggy-wants-to-fly). 바꾼 점: 글 없는 마지막 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: "I want to fly like the butterfly does."
"Follow me!" said the butterfly.
"But I do not have wings. I cannot fly."
"I know! I'll use palm leaves to make wings!"
"Flap your wings hard to fly!" cried the butterfly.
"I cannot seem to fly," said Piggy. "Let me try one more time."
"Look! I can fly!" Piggy said, leaping off the branch.
"Oh no! Why did I fall? I do not have wings like you, so I will have to be okay with not flying."

stories.title: Where Is My Bat?
stories.credit: "Where Is My Bat?" by Meera Tendolkar, translated by Madhav Chavan, (c) Pratham Books 2024, illustrated by Kabini Amin, (c) Kabini Amin 2024, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/621383-where-is-my-bat). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I have lost my bat, and I cannot find it.
I looked behind the door. It was not there.
I looked for it on the shelf. I could not find it there.
I looked for it under the bed. Not there either.
I searched inside the box. There was no sign of it.
I searched the attic. I could not find it anywhere. I looked here, there and everywhere.
Oh! There's my bat!

stories.title: Lost and Found
stories.credit: "Lost and Found" written and illustrated by Sukhada Rahalkar, (c) Pratham Books 2014, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/356-lost-and-found). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Not here, not there. Where have you gone?
Not on the sofa. Not under the cot.
Not in the box. Not under my sister's frock.
Not under the pillow. Not in my bag. Sob, sob, where have you gone?
I have looked in every room. I have looked under every book.
I have looked under the chair. I have looked under the stool. Where have you gone?
Soon Granny came back from her walk. "Look what I found in the park."
"It can sway, it can bounce. It can spin, it can dangle. Ha-ha, hee-hee," said Granny with a giggle.
Oh Granny! Thank you so much! You have found my dear yo-yo!
"Yo-yo? What a funny name! What a funny toy! I want to play with it. It gives me so much joy!"
Giggle, giggle, giggling away, Granny played with my little toy for the rest of the day!

stories.title: Look at Me
stories.credit: "Look at Me" by Pankaj Chaturvedi, translated by Manisha Chaudhry, illustrated by Ajit Narayan, (c) Pratham Books 2006, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/184-look-at-me). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Look at us. Do you want to be our friend?
My legs are very strong. I can run really fast with them.
And my arms... such a nice swing!
I like to draw. I use my hands for drawing.
Should I draw your picture? I can see you with my eyes.
The bird sings a sweet song. I can hear it with my ears.
I think Ma is making halwa. I can smell it with my nose.
Oh! This sugarcane is so tough! But my teeth are strong too!
It is very sweet. My tongue just told me.
I can sing. Should I sing you a song?
Ma says I have a good voice. Does it come from my throat?

stories.title: Who Is Our Friend?
stories.credit: "Who Is Our Friend?" written by Jade Mathieson, illustrated by Gerhard Van Wyk, (c) Book Dash 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/24795-who-is-our-friend). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고 글 없는 쪽을 뺐으며, 음성 안전검사가 잘못 걸러 낸 두 문장(벼룩을 먹는다·쪼아 청소한다)을 'picks them all off', 'cleans them all'로 바꿈, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Can you guess who our best friend is? He's not like us at all.
Our best friend is Bird!
I am Rhino. I get covered in fleas.
Bird picks them all off.
I am Crocodile. I can't brush my teeth.
Bird cleans them all.
I am Giraffe. I can't scratch my head.
Bird can reach just the right spot.
I am Zebra. I can't see things far away.
Bird has great eyes, so when he's watching, I'm safe.
Bird might be different, but that's no problem...
We don't even mind when he sings!
Will you be my friend?

stories.title: Tumi Goes to the Park
stories.credit: "Tumi Goes to the Park" written by Paballo Rampa, illustrated by Nyambura Kariuki, (c) Book Dash 2017, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/18402-tumi-goes-to-the-park). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고 글 없는 쪽 4개를 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: It's Tumi's first trip to the park.
"Mama, what's that?"
"It's a slide," says Mama. "May I go on it?" asks Tumi. "Of course!" says Mama.
"Wheeeee!"
"Look, Mama, I swing like a monkey."
"I just went past you ten times, Mama!" says Tumi. "Clever girl!" says Mama. "You know how to count!"
"Do you want to play?" asks Tumi. "Yes!" says the boy.
"I'm Tumi." "I'm Zakhe."
Tumi sees the sandpit. "Let's build a sandcastle!" says Tumi.
"I'm taking a photo for Gogo," says Mama.
"It's time to go home now, Tumi," says Mama. "Bye, Zakhe!" waves Tumi. "Bye, Tumi!" says Zakhe. "See you next time!"
"Mama, thank you for bringing me to the park," says Tumi.

stories.title: Rat and Goat
stories.credit: "Rat and Goat" by Ley Sorya, translated by Sanjana Khoobchandani, illustrated by Try Samphors, (c) Room to Read 2014, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/36678-rat-and-goat). 바꾼 점: 캄보디아 놀이 이름 'Moek'을 빼고 'hopscotch'만 남겼으며, 글 없는 쪽 2개를 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Rat loves to play outside.
Today he wants to play hopscotch, but there is nobody to play with.
"I have an idea," he thinks. "I'll invite Goat, my neighbour."
Goat likes to spend time alone, fishing and napping.
Rat goes to Goat's house and knocks on the door. Tok, tok!
"Brother Goat!" Rat exclaims. "Come play with me!"
"No, no!" Goat says. "I need to sleep. I don't want to play."
"Please, Goat," Rat replies. "Play with me. We will have fun together."
Finally, Goat agrees. "Okay, okay," Goat says. "I will play with you."
Goat and Rat play hopscotch together.
Goat has lots of fun playing with Rat. He decides that next time, he will jump out of bed to play.

stories.title: My Best Friend
stories.credit: "My Best Friend" written by Anupa Lal, illustrated by Suvidha Mistry, (c) Pratham Books 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/1042-my-best-friend). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I have a friend. She lives in my house.
When I am happy, so is she.
When I cry, she cries too.
But I cannot hear her voice. My friend lives inside the mirror.
"Come out," I tell her, "we will play." She does not come out.
I am not happy. I go to sleep.
She comes out of the mirror in my sleep! And we have fun.
We play, we run, we shout and scream together.
When I talk to her, she also talks to me.
In the morning, my friend will go back into the mirror.
But I don't mind at all. We will play again in my dreams!

stories.title: I Can Help!
stories.credit: "I Can Help!" written by Mini Shrinivasan, illustrated by Aman Randhawa, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/968-i-can-help). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I am a big girl. I can help other people.
After school, I like to feed my brother. He loves it.
When I have a holiday, I help my mother to get ready to go to the office.
In the evening, I help my father in his shop.
But sometimes my mother says, "Please, do not help me!"
And sometimes my father says, "Thank you, but please do not help me today."
Sometimes they both tell me to sit in one place. I like to read a book then!
I like to help my grandmother. She tells me stories.
My brother is still small. He cannot help at all.
But I am a big girl.
I can help other people.

stories.title: Is There Anyone Like Me?
stories.credit: "Is There Anyone Like Me?" written by Fred Strydom, illustrated by Jess Jardim-Wedepohl, (c) African Storybook Initiative 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/15136-is-there-anyone-like-me). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I wonder if there's another me somewhere in the world.
Who looks the same.
And talks the same.
And even has my curls.
Someone with my eyes, my ears.
Who even has my laugh.
Who can do what I can do.
And can't do what I can't.
I've looked and looked everywhere to find another me. I went down to the park and looked behind the trees.
I looked around, up and down.
At every single face.
I couldn't find another me in any single place.
There's only one me in the world! I'm special, oh it's true!
But not just me, don't you see? There's only one of you!

stories.title: The Moon and the Cap
stories.credit: Adapted from "The Moon and The Cap" by Rohini Nilekani, illustrated by Angie & Upesh, (c) Pratham Books 2007, CC BY 4.0 (storyweaver.org.in). 아이 눈높이로 문장을 고쳐 썼고 그림은 bilody가 새로 그림.

pages.text: Look. A cap. A blue cap. Mama gives me a blue cap. I put on my cap. My cap is soft and blue. I like my blue cap.
Oh! The wind blows. Whoosh, whoosh. The wind is strong. The wind takes my cap. Up, up, up. Where is my cap? Whoosh goes the wind.
Look. A tree. A big tall tree. My cap is up in the tree. The tree holds my cap. My cap sits in the tree.
It is night. Look up. The moon. A bright moon. The moon sees my cap. The moon smiles. Do you see the moon? Hello, moon.
The moon puts on my cap. Look. The moon has a blue cap. The cap fits the moon. A happy moon. I smile at the moon.
Look. A new cap. A red cap. Mama says it is from the moon. Now I have a cap. The moon has a cap. Good night, moon.

stories.title: Who Can?
stories.credit: Adapted from "Can and Can't" by Radha HS, illustrated by Ruchi Shah, (c) Pratham Books 2010, CC BY 4.0 (storyweaver.org.in). 아이 눈높이로 문장을 고쳐 썼고 그림은 bilody가 새로 그림.

pages.text: Look. A fish. A little fish. The fish can swim. Swim, swim, swim. The fish swims and swims. Do you see the fish?
Look up. A bird. A little blue bird. The bird can fly. Fly, fly, fly. Up and up goes the bird.
Look. A dog. A happy dog. The dog can bark. Woof, woof. The dog can run too. Run, run, little dog.
Look. A cat. A soft cat. The cat can jump. Jump, jump. Up jumps the cat. What a big jump, little cat.
Look. A monkey. A funny monkey. The monkey can swing. Swing, swing, swing. Hold on, little monkey.
Look. A pig. A pink pig. The pig can eat. Yum, yum, yum. And I can clap. Clap, clap, clap. Bye-bye, little pig.

stories.title: The Weather Report
stories.credit: "The Weather Report" written and illustrated by Vishnu M Nair, (c) Pratham Books 2021, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/266189-the-weather-report). 바꾼 점: 쪽 번호와 글 없는 쪽 하나를 빼고 ‘overcast’를 ‘grey’로, ‘ENOUGH’를 ‘Enough’로 바꿈, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Time for the weather report!
Today, the weather is sunny...
and so very hot!
Today the weather is rainy...
and so very wet.
Today it’s cloudy and grey.
Today it was windy...
and now it’s stormy!
And today? It’s cold.
Enough!
Oh, today? Today the weather is just right.

stories.title: Hide and Seek
stories.credit: "Hide and Seek" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Harshvardhan Gantha, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/12292-hide-and-seek). 바꾼 점: 그림 없는 1쪽에는 2쪽 그림을, 9쪽에는 앞 쪽 그림을 쓰고 ‘1-2-3’을 ‘One, two, three’로 풀어 씀, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Jeetu is playing with his friends.
It is Jeetu’s turn to count till a hundred.
Jeetu has started counting.
Viju hides behind a tree.
Raju hides near the car.
Suman hides behind a door.
Aman hides under a basket.
Biju hides inside a drum.
Oh, no! Jeetu has stopped. Which number comes after 39?
Once more he starts counting. One, two, three. His friends must hide again.

stories.title: My Friends
stories.credit: "My Friends" by Rukmini Banerji, translated by Manisha Chaudhry, illustrated by Rajeev Verma 'Banjara', (c) Pratham Books 2006, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/376-my-friends). 바꾼 점: 띄어쓰기를 고치고 느낌표 셋을 하나로 줄임, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I have many friends.
Some of my friends are older and...
some of them are younger than me.
Some of my friends are old.
And some of them are tiny!
Some of my friends have tails...
Some of my friends have no feet.
Some of my friends fly. Some of them swim.
Oh! Books are my friends too!
But who is my best friend? Who? Who? Who?
My mother!

stories.title: The Greedy Mouse
stories.credit: "The Greedy Mouse" written and illustrated by Herminder Ohri, (c) Pratham Books 2006, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/14406-the-greedy-mouse). 바꾼 점: ‘MOUSE’를 ‘Mouse’로, ‘stomach’을 ‘tummy’로 바꾸고 9쪽 한 문장(The bun was safely in his house)을 빼고 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: One day, Mouse found a very big bun. “I will take this bun into my house,” he said.
He pushed the bun from the back. It did not move.
He pushed it from the front. The bun did not move.
He pushed it from the right. The bun did not move.
He ran around the bun and pushed it from the left, but it still did not move.
Hmm... I will tie a string around the bun and pull it into my house. Mouse ran to the house and got a string, but it was too short.
He went back and got a longer string. He tied the bun with the long string, then pulled and pulled, but it did not move.
Mouse sat down and ate a little bit of the bun. It was very good. He ate a little more, then a little more, and a little more, till the bun became smaller and smaller.
He pushed the bun, and it rolled right into his house. Mouse was very happy. But he had eaten so much bun that his tummy had become so... so... big.
Mouse pushed and pushed himself, but he could not get into his house.
Mouse sat outside his door holding his tummy. “I should not have eaten so much bun. I should have shared it with someone.”

stories.title: Timmy and Pepe
stories.credit: "Timmy and Pepe" written by Madhav Chavan, illustrated by Santosh Pujari, (c) Pratham Books 2004, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/149-timmy-and-pepe). 바꾼 점: 그림 찾기 문제 쪽(마지막 쪽)을 빼고, 길게 늘인 흉내말을 줄이고 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I am Timmy. This is my friend, Pepe, the puppy.
I like to tease Pepe. I tell him I am better than him. He does not like it.
“Look, I have a nose!” I say. “Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has a nose too.
“Look, I have ears!” I say. “Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has ears too.
“Look, I have eyes!” I say. “Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has eyes too.
“Look, I can dance on my legs!” I say. “Woof, woof, woof,” says Pepe. That means he has legs too.
“Look, I have a tongue!” I say. “Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has a tongue too.
“I can think!” I say. “Woooof,” says Pepe. That means he can think better.
“Look, I have hands!” I say. “Grrr...” Pepe says, and turns to show his little tail. That means he has a tail and I don’t have one.
But I love Pepe, the puppy, and he loves me too.

stories.title: Bed-Time Stories
stories.credit: "Bed-Time Stories" written by Kanchan Bannerjee, illustrated by Harshvardhan Gantha, (c) Pratham Books 2013, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/12293-bed-time-stories). 바꾼 점: 그대로, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: My Amma tells me a story every night.
There is one story about a frog which talks.
There is another story about a king with a long beard.
Sometimes it is about a flying elephant.
In one story a fox and a tiger are friends. The tiger falls into a hole.
How will the tiger get out?
Then the clever fox saves the tiger. This is the best story. I listen to the story and then fall asleep.

stories.title: How Many?
stories.credit: "How Many?" written by Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla and Zanele Buthelezi, illustrated by Sandra McDougall, (c) African Storybook Initiative 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/15050-how-many). 바꾼 점: 그대로, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: How many legs do two ladybirds have?
How many wings do four birds have?
How many horns do three rhinos have?
How many trunks do five elephants have?
How many ears do seven dogs have?
How many tails do three monkeys have?
How many eyes do six cats have?
How many legs does one worm have?

stories.title: Tall and Short
stories.credit: "Tall and Short" by Huy Chheng Rattana, translated by Celia Bolam, illustrated by Seat Sopheap, (c) Room to Read 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/37230-tall-and-short). 바꾼 점: 글 없는 마지막 쪽을 빼고 이름 표기(JoJo)를 맞춤, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Pa is getting my hat.
Pa is tall.
Ma is getting my shirt.
Pa is taller than Ma.
My sister is getting my book.
Ma is taller than my sister.
My brother is getting my bag.
My sister is taller than my brother.
And my brother is taller than me.
I’m the shortest in the family.
Oh wait! There is our puppy, JoJo.
JoJo is getting my slippers.
Ha ha! JoJo is the shortest.
Yes! JoJo is shorter than me.
I’m shorter than my brother.
My brother is shorter than my sister.
My sister is shorter than Ma.
Ma is shorter than Pa.
Wow! Pa is the tallest, and JoJo is the shortest.

stories.title: The Red Raincoat
stories.credit: "The Red Raincoat" written by Kiran Kasturia, illustrated by Zainab Tambawalla, (c) Pratham Books 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/369-the-red-raincoat). 바꾼 점: 따옴표 앞뒤 띄어쓰기를 고치고 대문자 강조(WILL·WHEN·WHY·WHAT)를 보통 글씨로 바꿈, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: On Sunday, Manu’s parents got him a red raincoat. “Ma, may I wear it now?” asked Manu. “No, my dear, the rains are near, but just now the sky is clear,” said Ma.
Monday was bright and sunny. “Will it rain today, Mummy?” asked Manu. “No Manu, not today. If you wear your raincoat, you will look quite funny!” said Ma.
On Tuesday, the sky was blue. “Ma, when will my wish come true?” asked Manu. “Not today, my dear, there is just one white cloud in the sky!” said Ma.
Wednesday was hot. “Ma, why doesn’t it rain?” asked Manu. “Son, I think it will rain very soon. Maybe even before it is noon,” said Ma.

On Thursday Manu went on a picnic. “Ma, what if it rains? Shall I take the raincoat with me?” asked Manu. “No my dear, it will not rain today. The little white clouds are too high in the sky,” said Ma.
Friday was cloudy. “Ma, will it rain today?” asked Manu loudly. “It might, my dear. There are some dark clouds low down in the sky,” said Ma.
Saturday began with a bang! Badaboom! “Ma, is that thunder I hear? Will it rain very soon?” asked Manu.
And then at last, it started raining! “Oh, it’s raining, it’s raining,” sang Manu, running out.
“But Manu,” called Ma, running after him, “you forgot your raincoat!”

stories.title: The Little Leaf
stories.credit: "The Little Leaf" by Prayag Shukla, translated by Swagata Sen Pillai, illustrated by Sonal Goyal, (c) Pratham Books 2018, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/47926-the-little-leaf). 바꾼 점: 시의 줄 나눔을 문장으로 이어 문장부호를 넣음(낱말은 그대로), 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: A little blue-green leaf fell off the tree. A squirrel came running and ran over it. Wheee!
A bird sat upon it, flapped and flew away! A breeze lifted the leaf in the air, from where it lay!
Just then the skies opened. A few raindrops fell. The little leaf shook. It was scared, one could tell. A little boy came and picked up the leaf. He dusted it off and wiped the mud clean!
“How pretty this is,” he thought to himself, and pasted it in the book kept on the shelf!

stories.title: Friends
stories.credit: "Friends" written by Hlengiwe Zondi and Zimbili Dlamini, illustrated by Catherine Groenewald, (c) African Storybook Initiative 2014, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/14806-friends). 바꾼 점: 그대로, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: My name is Simo.
I have four friends.
Their names are Zizo, Lele, Sisa and Ayanda.
My friend Zizo likes to play soccer.
My friend Lele likes to swim.
My friend Sisa likes to play hide-and-seek.
My friend Ayanda likes to read.
Me? I like to do the things they like to do.
I play soccer with Zizo.
I swim with Lele.
I play hide-and-seek with Sisa.
Come, friend, what do you like?
Come, play soccer with us.
Come, swim with us.
Come, play hide-and-seek with us.
Come, read with us!

stories.title: Smile Please!
stories.credit: "Smile Please!" by Sanjiv Jaiswal 'Sanjay', translated by Manisha Chaudhry, illustrated by Ajit Narayan, (c) Pratham Books 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/2-smile-please). 바꾼 점: 8쪽 문장(monkey massaged…tears flowed)을 음성 안전검사 때문에 ‘The monkey rubbed his leg. The fawn was still crying.’로 바꾸고, 10쪽 ‘we’ll beat up this bad boulder’를 ‘we’ll scold this bad boulder’로 순하게 바꾸고, 글 없는 마지막 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: A fawn was racing in the forest.
He was ahead of the rabbit.
He was ahead of the elephant.
He leapt and cleared the stream.
He ran past the crumbling wall.
There was a large boulder on the grassy plain. He stumbled and fell down.
He burst into tears.
The monkey rubbed his leg. The fawn was still crying.
Brother Bear picked him up. The fawn didn’t stop crying.
His mother came. She said, “Look, we’ll scold this bad boulder!”
The fawn said, “Oh, don’t do that or he will also start crying.” His mother laughed. So did the fawn.

stories.title: Bath Time for Chunnu and Munnu
stories.credit: "Bath Time for Chunnu and Munnu" written by Rohini Nilekani, (c) StoryWeaver 2015, English translation by Rohini Nilekani, illustrated by Sonal Goyal and Sumit Sakhuja, (c) Pratham Books 2015, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/6100-bath-time-for-chunnu-and-munnu). 바꾼 점: 노랫말 줄 나눔을 문장으로 이어 문장부호를 넣고, ‘Thup’을 ‘Pop’으로, ‘Nana and Nani’를 ‘Grandpa and Grandma’로, ‘tying up pyjamas’를 ‘putting on pyjamas’로 바꿈, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Yay! It is bath time for Chunnu and Munnu. Today, Mama sings a new rhyme for Chunnu and Munnu. La la la la...
It is bath time for Chunnu and Munnu. Mama washes all the dirt off Chunnu and Munnu. Scrub-a-dub-dub...
It is bath time for Chunnu and Munnu. Soap bubbles and fun for Chunnu and Munnu. Pop! Pop! Pop!
It is bath time for Chunnu and Munnu. Mama runs to catch naughty Chunnu and Munnu. Ha ha ha ha...
Bath time is over for Chunnu and Munnu. Mama hugs clean, clean Chunnu and Munnu. Mmm...
Bath time is over for Chunnu and Munnu. But putting on pyjamas is hard for Chunnu and Munnu. Oh, oh, ah...
Bath time is over for Chunnu and Munnu. Yay! It is dinner time for Chunnu and Munnu. Yum, yum, yum...
Dinner time is over for Chunnu and Munnu. Grandpa and Grandma are waiting to kiss Chunnu and Munnu. Mwah, mwah, mwah...
Play time is over for Chunnu and Munnu. Sweet dreams now for Chunnu and Munnu. Zzz...

stories.title: Animal Homes
stories.credit: "Animal Homes" written by Ashwitha Jayakumar, illustrated by Nafisa Nandini Crishna, (c) Pratham Books 2019, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/61292-animal-homes). 바꾼 점: 쪽 번호와 마지막 쪽 소제목(One Large Home)·물음 한 문장을 빼고 이어지게 고쳐 씀, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Animals live all around us.
Birds build their homes up high. And so do bees.
Spiders spin their homes. Tiny termites build tall, tall homes.
Snails and tortoises grow homes on their backs.
Fish live in the water. Frogs can live in water and on land.
Rabbits and rats live in burrows under the ground.
Monkeys and apes make trees their homes.
Bears and wolves live in dens.
Crocodiles live in swamps.
Deer live in forests. And so do tigers!
Some animals live close to us and some live far away. But we all build our homes in one large home: planet Earth!

stories.title: Little Sock and the Tiny Creatures
stories.credit: "Little Sock and the Tiny Creatures" written by Jon Keevy, (c) Book Dash 2016, illustrated by Lili Probart, (c) Lili Probart 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/13919-little-sock-and-the-tiny-creatures). 바꾼 점: 양말 인형 만들기 쪽과 글 없는 마지막 두 쪽을 뺌, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: It’s wash day for the Socks.
Oh no! Little Sock falls out!
“I have to get home,” says Little Sock.
“Do you know the way home?” asks Little Sock.
“No, but take this,” says the Robot.
“Do you know the way home?” asks Little Sock.
“No, but take this,” says the Mouse.
“Do you know the way home?” asks Little Sock.
“No, but take... Oops!”
“Maybe the marble knows the way home,” says Little Sock.
“It does!” says Little Sock.
Little Sock is happy.

stories.title: I Love My Mom
stories.credit: "I Love My Mom" by Fongsamay Phommaxay, translated by Stephanie Wei, illustrated by Nivong Sengsakoun, (c) Room to Read 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/36490-i-love-my-mom). 바꾼 점: 소리 흉내말(WHEEEEEEE)을 ‘Wheee’로 줄임, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: My mom’s name is Lee. She works hard all the time. And I learn so much from her!
When my mom cooks, I learn to cook too.
When she waters the flowers, I learn to water the flowers too.
When she washes our clothes, I learn to wash our clothes too.
When she dries our clothes, I learn to dry our clothes too.
My mom also bought me a bicycle, and she taught me how to ride it.
As I ride my bicycle, my mom smiles when I go “Wheee!”
At night, my mom makes the bed. I learn how to make the bed too.
Before bedtime, my mom tells me stories.
When I’m sleepy, my mom sings me a lullaby.
I love my mom so much!

stories.title: The Roti Roll
stories.credit: "The Roti Roll" by Amar Goswami, translated by Manisha Chaudhry, illustrated by Partho Sengupta, (c) Pratham Books 2006, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/60812-the-roti-roll). 바꾼 점: 힌디어 흉내말(Bhaun·Kaanv)을 영어 흉내말(Woof·Caw)로, ‘pipal tree’를 ‘big tree’로 바꾸고 2~4쪽 문장을 조금 줄이고 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Kamal had a dog. He was called Bhaunkoo.
One day, Kamal gave Bhaunkoo a roti. Down came a monkey and snatched the roti away! He climbed up the wall to eat it.
A crow saw the roti. He swooped down and took the roti before the monkey could take a bite. He flew to the big tree in the courtyard.
There was a peacock in the tree. He saw the roti too. Bhaunkoo barked loudly, “Woof, woof, woof, woof!”
The crow got scared. He cawed, “Caw, caw!”
As he opened his beak, the roti fell down. It fell in the courtyard.
Bhaunkoo snapped it up at once. The roti was back where it belonged!

stories.title: Hippo Wants to Dance
stories.credit: "Hippo Wants to Dance" written by Marisa Steyn and Sam Beckbessinger, illustrated by Megan Andrews, (c) Book Dash 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/24737-hippo-wants-to-dance). 바꾼 점: 글 없는 쪽 셋(처음 하나, 끝 둘)을 빼고, 음성 안전검사 때문에 11쪽 문장을 ‘Watch out! You almost stepped on us! says Meerkat.’로 바꾸고 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Hippo wants to dance. She jumps up and down on the dusty ground.
Thump! Thump!
“You’re getting dirt on me!” says Shongololo, sleeping in the sand.
“Go dance somewhere else.”
Hippo wants to dance. She rolls into the river and splashes her arms and legs.
Splish! Splash!
“You’re making me wet!” says Kingfisher, hunting for her breakfast.
“Go dance somewhere else.”
Hippo wants to dance. She twirls around and around in a field, kicking her legs up high.
Swoosh! Swoosh!
“Watch out! You almost stepped on us!” says Meerkat.
“Go dance somewhere else.”
Hippo wants to dance. She flops into a puddle of mud and slides around on her nice big belly.
Squish! Squash!
“Why don’t you stop dancing?” asks Donkey, carrying his buckets.
“Why can’t you do something useful instead?”
Hippo is sad. She is too sad to dance.
She sits on a rock and cries. The tears roll down her cheeks and fall on the ground.
Plop! Plop! Grasshopper hears Hippo’s tears. He starts dancing around her feet.
Hop! Hop!
Hippo and Grasshopper start to dance, and the other animals come to look...

stories.title: Houses
stories.credit: "Houses" written by Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla and Zanele Buthelezi, (c) African Storybook Initiative 2007, illustrated by Kathy Arbuckle, (c) Kathy Arbuckle and African Storybook Initiative 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/14833-houses). 바꾼 점: 그대로, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Mzi lives in a thatched house.
Thulani lives in a square house.
This house is a rectangle.
The roof of this house is a triangle.
This man is building his own house.
This house is new.
This house is old.
I wish I lived in this house.

stories.title: Chhuk-Chhuk-Chhak
stories.credit: "Chhuk-Chhuk-Chhak" by Vinita Krishna, translated by Ritu Singh, illustrated by Suvidha Mistry, (c) Pratham Books 2006, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/240-chhuk-chhuk-chhak). 바꾼 점: ‘l-o-n-g’을 ‘long, long’으로, ‘make the coaches’를 ‘draw the coaches’로, ‘chalk got over’를 ‘chalk ran out’으로, ‘verandah’를 ‘porch’로, 기차 소리를 ‘Choo-choo, chug-chug’로 바꿈, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Nanhi picked up her slate and chalk. She wanted to draw a long, long train.
Nanhi first drew an engine which gave out a lot of smoke, for the long, long train.
“Oh dear! Now where shall I draw the coaches?” Nanhi wondered, for there was no more space on the slate.
Nanhi put the slate and chalk down on the floor and thought.
She drew a coach on the floor. Then a second coach, then another, and another, and another... Nanhi just kept drawing.
Until her chalk ran out. Nanhi got up and took a look. Wow! Her train was as long as the porch!
And off went Nanhi’s train. Choo-choo, chug-chug! From here to there, so very far!

stories.title: Too Big! Too Small!
stories.credit: "Too Big! Too Small!" written and illustrated by Lavanya Karthik, (c) Pratham Books 2017, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/16411-too-big-too-small). 바꾼 점: 붙어 있던 낱말 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: “I can’t lift you up, Shanu!” says Ammi. “You are too big!”
“You can’t walk to school alone, Shanu!” says Abbu. “You are too small!”
“You can’t sleep in the baby’s cot, Shanu!” says Dadu. “You are too big!”
“You can’t carry the baby to the park, Shanu!” says Dadi. “You are too small!”
Shanu is puzzled. Too big! Too small! How can she be too big and too small all at once?
Too big to wear her old pink frock. Too small to make dosas at the stove.
Too big to climb up on Dadu’s back? Too small to carry the baby on hers?
“What am I the right size for?” Shanu wonders.
Ammi smiles and says, “Why, you are just big enough to go to big school.”
“And you are just small enough for me to carry you on my shoulders,” says Abbu.
“You are just big enough to take me for my morning walks,” says Dadu.
“And you are just small enough for me to tell stories to,” says Dadi.
“And you will always, always be the perfect size... for this!” all say, and give her a warm, wonderful hug.

stories.title: My Home
stories.credit: "My Home" by Rukmini Banerji, translated by Manisha Chaudhry, illustrated by Rajeev Verma 'Banjara', (c) Pratham Books 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/288-my-home). 바꾼 점: 그대로, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: This is my home.
I live here with my whole family.
We take off our shoes and chappals here.
This is where we wash our face and hands.
I hang my clothes on the hook.
My grandfather keeps his stick in the corner.
We also keep our mats there.
My father keeps his motorcycle outside.
But his helmet is on the cupboard.
My mother and grandmother keep their saris in the trunk.
Tasty food is cooked in the kitchen.
When it is cold, we bring out quilts.
When it is hot, we use a fan.
When we have important guests, we bring out the chairs.
You must come and visit my home. Come soon.

stories.title: Lara the Yellow Ladybird
stories.credit: "Lara the Yellow Ladybird" written by Catherine Holtzhausen, Martha Evans and Nadene Kriel, (c) Book Dash 2016, illustrated by Catherine Holtzhausen, (c) Catherine Holtzhausen 2016, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/13916-lara-the-yellow-ladybird). 바꾼 점: 글 없는 마지막 두 쪽을 빼고 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Lara the ladybird was a special bug.
Unlike all her friends, she had bright yellow wings.
Everyone loved her yellow wings.
Each morning, Bibi Butterfly said hello. And Manto Mantis always waved.
Even Sesa, the sulky spider, was happy to see her.
At school, she played with lots of friends.
But Lara wanted to be like the other ladybirds. “I wish I had red wings like you, Mama,” she cried.
So one day, to cheer her up, Lara’s mother painted her wings bright red.
The next morning, nobody greeted Lara on her way to school.
And when she got there, none of her friends said hello.
Lara sat all alone. No one noticed her new red wings.
Until Miss Miya spotted her and said, “You’ve painted your lovely yellow wings!”
Lara’s classmates were shocked. “Your wings are special!” “So unique!” “So rare!”
“Lara,” Miss Miya said, “your yellow wings are what make you you. Like Sipho’s spot, and Sally’s legs.”
Back home, Lara took a long bath and scrubbed until her golden wings gleamed.
“I’ll never paint my wings again!” she thought. Except, maybe once or twice...
To try a bit of purple, or something nice. But not for ever, and just for fun.

stories.title: Little Painters
stories.credit: "Little Painters" written by Cheryl Rao, illustrated by Tanvi Bhat, (c) Pratham Books 2012, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/218-little-painters). 바꾼 점: 문장부호만 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: It was holiday time. Veena and Vinay were in the garden. There were tins of paint everywhere.
There was white paint and red paint and green paint and blue paint and yellow paint.
The painters were busy. One painter was on a ladder. Another was hanging from the roof on a swing. “Can we help?” asked Veena and Vinay.
The painter gave each of them a brush. “Paint the inside of the gate,” he said to Veena. “Paint the outside of the gate,” he said to Vinay.
They picked up two tins of paint and set to work. Veena painted one side of the gate. Vinay painted the other side of the gate.
The paint fell on the ground. The paint fell on the wall. The paint fell on them.
At last they finished. They wiped off the paint that had splashed on the ground. They wiped off the paint that had splashed on the wall.
They wiped off the paint that had splashed on them.
“I love my red gate!” said Veena.
“I love my green gate!” said Vinay.
“Oh, you have made a two-coloured gate!” cried the painter. “Let us keep it that way!” said Mother.

stories.title: Who Is Faster?
stories.credit: "Who Is Faster?" by Shilpi Pradhan, translated by Rose Larsen, illustrated by Kishor Joshi, (c) Room to Read 2007, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/42989-who-is-faster). 바꾼 점: 두 쪽에 걸친 물음 세 개를 한 쪽으로 합치고(그 그림 세 장은 뺌) 띄어쓰기를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: Do you know which animal is the slowest in the world?
The tortoise.
Who is faster than the tortoise?
The snake.
Who is faster than the tortoise and the snake?
The mouse.
Who is faster than the tortoise, the snake, and the mouse?
The lizard.
Who is faster than the tortoise, the snake, the mouse, and the lizard?
The elephant.
Who is faster than the tortoise, the snake, the mouse, the lizard, and the elephant?
The cat.
Who is faster than the tortoise, the snake, the mouse, the lizard, the elephant, and the cat?
The jackal.
Who is faster than the tortoise, the snake, the mouse, the lizard, the elephant, the cat, and the jackal?
The rabbit.
Who is faster than the tortoise, the snake, the mouse, the lizard, the elephant, the cat, the jackal, and the rabbit?
The horse.
Who is faster than the tortoise, the snake, the mouse, the lizard, the elephant, the cat, the jackal, the rabbit, and the horse?
The leopard.

stories.title: Not Now, Not Now!
stories.credit: "Not Now, Not Now!" written by Rohini Nilekani, illustrated by Ruchi Shah, (c) Pratham Books 2011, CC BY 4.0, via StoryWeaver (storyweaver.org.in/en/stories/33-not-now-not-now). 바꾼 점: ‘Ajji·Ajja’를 ‘Grandma·Grandpa’로, ‘beta’를 ‘dear’로, ‘play cricket’을 ‘play’로 바꾸고(과자 이름 laddoos는 그대로) 문장부호를 고침, 그림 크기를 줄이고 토리 목소리로 읽음.

pages.text: I asked Grandma, “May I please have some laddoos?” “Not now, dear, maybe tomorrow.” But I did not want to wait till tomorrow.
I asked Grandpa, “May I go out to play with my friends?” “Not now, dear. Maybe after your nap?” But I did not want to wait till after my nap.
I asked Ma, “May I wear these new clothes?” “Not now, dear, you can wear them when we go out.” But I did not want to wait till we went out.
I asked Papa, “May I open that nice looking box?” “Not now, not now. You must wait.” But I did not want to wait any more.
Why do big people always say, ‘Not now, not now’? That night, I went to sleep feeling angry.
The next day, I woke up early and went into the kitchen. Grandma said, “You can eat these laddoos now.”
Grandpa said, “We can play now.” Ma said, “You can wear these clothes now.” Papa said, “You can open this box now.” And they all said, “Happy birthday!”

intro.text: Hi! It is story time. Look and listen with me.

end.text: The end. That was fun. Bye-bye!
